item.title: The Good, the Bad and the Cringe: 10 Ads That Defined the Midterms
item.author: Shane Goldmacher and Tim Balk
item.content:encoded: In a Democratic landslide election, here are the ads that stood out. Some were effective, while others backfired.

item.title: He’ll Be Clerk of One of the Country’s Largest Counties. He’s 19.
item.author: Mack Liederman
item.content:encoded: Sebastian Matta, a sophomore at Arizona State University, was elected on Tuesday as Superior Court clerk in Maricopa County, Ariz.

item.title: Mysterious Request Scrambles Major Supreme Court Gun Case Against Cook County
item.author: Abbie VanSickle
item.content:encoded: In an unusual move, the lead plaintiff in one of two cases challenging semiautomatic weapons bans has asked to drop out weeks before the cases are heard.

item.title: Democrats, Newly Ascendant, Begin a Fight to Shape the Party’s Future
item.author: Lisa Lerer and Reid J. Epstein
item.content:encoded: At a moment of opportunity for the party, its long-feuding factions are seizing on the midterm results to make their case for tacking to the center or to the left.

item.title: U.S. Cleared Nvidia Chips to Chinese Firms With Empty Offices and Troubling Ties
item.author: Ana Swanson, Kalley Huang and Keith Bradsher
item.content:encoded: The Commerce Department has approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia’s H200 chips, some of which have ties to firms under sanctions over national security.

item.title: With So Much New Blood in the Senate, the Average Age Is Falling. To 63.
item.author: Francesca Paris and C.J. Robinson
item.content:encoded: Incoming senators are nearly 15 years younger than departing ones, on average. But the chamber’s overall age isn’t shifting much.

item.title: Kyiv Faces Russian Missile Barrage, Naftogaz Facilities Damaged
item.author: Olesia Safronova
item.content:encoded: Ukraine’s capital and the region surrounding Kyiv faced another Russian missile barrage overnight targeting energy facilities and bridges, with at least one civilian killed and several injured.

item.title: Czech Premier Blasts Central Bank Rate Hike as ‘Scandalous’
item.author: Michal Kubala
item.content:encoded: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis stepped up his public criticism of the country’s central bank following this week’s interest-rate hike, calling the board’s decision “absolutely scandalous” and saying it will hurt households and companies.

item.title: Finland Considers Ukraine-Style Tank Barriers as Russia Rearms
item.author: Kirsi Heikel
item.content:encoded: In Ukraine, anti-tank obstacles have slowed the attacker. Now Finland wants to see how such structures would fare in harsh northern weather.

item.title: New Zealand Election Kingmaker Emerges With 50% of Vote Counted
item.author: Ainsley Thomson and Tracy Withers
item.content:encoded: New Zealand’s two main parties are neck-and-neck with half the votes counted in the nation’s election, but projections currently show both political blocs are may need the support of the centrist Opportunity Party, which is on track to enter parliament for the first time.

item.title: Burnham Bets That Britain Can Move Past the Old Brexit Divisions
item.author: Chloe Chaplain and Alex Wickham
item.content:encoded: In British politics, dividing lines have formed around Brexit for the past decade, often replacing traditional right-and-left allegiances. Now, Andy Burnham is backing himself to redraw the political map all over again.

item.title: Malaysian King Says No Ambiguity on Najib’s Home Detention Order
item.author: Liau Y-Sing
item.content:encoded: Malaysia’s king declared there was no ambiguity over his pardon for former Prime Minister Najib Razak, warning that any challenge to the decree amounts to defying his authority as the attorney general’s office calls for a delay in its implementation.

item.title: U.S. Homeless Population Had Record Drop in 2025
item.author: Jason DeParle
item.content:encoded: The Department of Housing and Urban Development credited President Trump, while homeless advocacy groups said that so-called Housing First policies of his predecessors played a part.

item.title: Trump’s D.C. Construction Blitz May Be About to Get Tougher
item.author: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
item.content:encoded: The president has bulldozed through obstacles as he has sought to remake the face of Washington. But newly empowered Democrats and angry judges are setting up a high-stakes showdown.

item.title: What to Know About Stephen Miller, Trump’s New Chief of Staff
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: The architect of President Trump’s mass deportation campaign, Mr. Miller has been the public face of many of Mr. Trump’s immigration policies.

item.title: Hong Kong Arrests 28 in Building Bid-Rigging Probe, RTHK Says
item.author: Aileen Chuang
item.content:encoded: Hong Kong authorities arrested 28 people tied to a suspected triad-linked bid-rigging syndicate targeting building maintenance and renovation contracts, Radio Television Hong Kong reported, citing Secretary for Security Chris Tang.

item.title: China’s Top Spy Agency Recruited Woman Who Targeted Jensen Huang
item.author: Julian E. Barnes, Tripp Mickle, Paul Mozur and Maggie Haberman
item.content:encoded: A memo that circulated among U.S. policymakers cited intelligence that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive who developed a relationship with Nvidia’s leader, was an asset of Beijing’s Ministry of State Security.

item.title: US Believes Woman Close to Nvidia CEO Was a China Spy, NYT Says
item.author: John Harney
item.content:encoded: US intelligence officials told the Trump administration that a woman who had become close to Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was working for a Chinese spy agency, which recruited her to collect information on him, the New York Times reported Friday.

item.title: In Elevating Stephen Miller, Trump Doubles Down on Hard-Line Agenda
item.author: Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan and Tyler Pager
item.content:encoded: The new White House chief of staff is responsible for some of the most provocative policies of President Trump’s second term, as well as an aggressive approach to executive power.

item.title: Australia’s Albanese Urges Iran De-Escalation After US Midterms
item.author: Richard Henderson
item.content:encoded: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has called for a de-escalation of tensions between the US and Iran after the midterm elections, which he described as “very significant,” according to a report from the Australian Broadcasting Corp.

item.title: Wall Street Week | Blue Wave Economic Impacts, European Welfare Woes
item.content:encoded: This week, Columbia Business School professor Glenn Hubbard breaks down the economic implications of the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, rising oil prices are both a burden and a benefit in Alaska. And, we go into the field with Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin to get a closer look at American manufacturing. Plus, Europe’s postwar welfare programs are facing new challenges amid budget crunches and growing youth protests. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Touts Plan for US Air Show, Seeks to Turn Page on Midterm
item.author: Kate Sullivan
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump sought to shrug off his Republican Party’s disastrous midterm defeat during a visit to Florida, touting plans to launch a new US air show as an example of how his economic agenda is revitalizing American industry.

item.title: Wiles Out as White House Chief of Staff, Stephen Miller Takes Role
item.content:encoded: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Joe Manchin, former US Senator and Governor for West Virginia, says Democrats can overplay their hand if they make impeaching President Donald Trump a priority after taking control of Congress. Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Susie Wiles Is the Latest Powerful Woman to Exit the Trump Administration
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: A wave of high-ranking women have left the Trump administration in the past year. Many were replaced by men.

item.title: Coinbase’s Ryan VanGrack Says Crypto Clarity Is Advancing
item.content:encoded: Coinbase Vice Chair Ryan VanGrack says legislation has stalled since the Clarity Act vote, but the SEC and CFTC are advancing regulatory measures that are providing another route to clarity. He added that crypto is inherently bipartisan, even as regulatory proposals may face congressional scrutiny and debate. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Chip Stocks Rebound
item.content:encoded:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December. Technology stocks staged a sharp recovery, but whether that holds is another matter. Meantime, President Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles will move to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bremmer: U.S. Retreat From Global Leadership Is a Long-Term Shift
item.content:encoded: Ian Bremmer says Tuesday’s election should be viewed against structural changes in U.S. policy that are likely to persist regardless of which party holds the White House. He cites weaker support for free-trade agreements and a greater reliance on industrial policy, subsidies and tariffs. Bremmer speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Took Over Texas. What Now?
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: Democrats’ wins in the Lone Star state exceeded their wildest dreams.

item.title: Affordability First, Open to Hegseth Impeachment: Rep. Moore
item.content:encoded: Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. Rep. Moore says Democrats' agenda should not be “first and foremost” to impeach people, but says she will not push for impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and that it would be “hard not to vote yes” on Rep. Thomas Massie's privileged resolution. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Beyer: Democrats Were Not Elected to Impeach Trump
item.content:encoded: Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Beyer says he is depending on the courts and public sentiment to stop the project and has legislation aimed at preventing it from moving forward. Rep. Beyer says Democrats were not elected to impeach President Trump, but to stop the war and bring health care back to Americans. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Manchin: Democrats Risk Overplaying Hand on Impeachment
item.content:encoded: Joe Manchin, former US Senator and Governor for West Virginia, says Democrats can overplay their hand if they make impeaching President Donald Trump a priority after taking control of Congress. Manchin says Democrats should instead pass legislation addressing tariffs and public officials profiting from their positions and “try everything possible to put the genie back in the bottle.” Manchin says Trump will have to work with Congress because executive orders “only go so far and only last so long.” He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paraguayan President Peña Removed From Office, Arrested
item.author: Ken Parks
item.content:encoded: Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office Friday, a dramatic downfall that paves the way for him to face potential criminal charges over his alleged role in the collapse of a major bank.

item.title: Susie Wiles, Trump’s Chief of Staff, Is Accused of Blocking Health Policies to Attract Donations
item.author: Christina Jewett and Sheryl Gay Stolberg
item.content:encoded: In a no-holds-barred interview with Joe Rogan, Calley Means, a former top health adviser, accused Susie Wiles of repeatedly bowing to lobbying pressures and fixating on campaign contributions.

item.title: Hegseth Faces Impeachment Effort and Bipartisan Scrutiny After Midterm Elections
item.author: Helene Cooper, Greg Jaffe and Eric Schmitt
item.content:encoded: A looming impeachment push could put President Trump’s polarizing defense secretary in a standoff with Democrats and Republicans.

item.title: How Elon Musk Frittered Away Nearly $500 Million on the Midterm Elections
item.author: Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: Behind the scenes, the world’s richest person spent a record amount over two years to bend the country’s politics to his will. He couldn’t.

item.title: Christopher Murphy Will Not Return to Senate Next Week After Stroke
item.author: Michael Gold
item.content:encoded: Senator Christopher S. Murphy, Democrat of Connecticut, said in a statement that he would spend several weeks recovering at a rehabilitation center.

item.title: Amazon Follows Melania Trump Film With Two-Part Series by the Same Director
item.author: Marc Tracy
item.content:encoded: The documentary, which the first lady executive produces, will debut on Nov. 20. Brett Ratner directs.

item.title: Trump Taps Stephen Miller to Replace Wiles as Chief of Staff
item.author: Jeff Mason and Courtney Subramanian
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles is moving to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result.

item.title: U.S. Attorney Who Oversaw Centerpiece of Trump’s Revenge Campaign Resigns
item.author: Devlin Barrett, Glenn Thrush and Alan Feuer
item.content:encoded: Jason Reding Quiñones joins what is expected to be a succession of departures at the Justice Department after the midterm elections, including that of the leader of the national security division.

item.title: U.S. Global Health Strategy Jeopardizes Prevention of Pandemics, Experts Warn
item.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has been negotiating agreements with dozens of individual countries. Public health experts say a global agreement would be far more effective.

item.title: John D. Rockefeller IV, West Virginia Governor and Senator, Dies at 89
item.author: Robert D. McFadden
item.content:encoded: The rare Democrat in a fabled family of wealthy Republicans, he served 30 years as senator and helped bring health insurance to millions of low-income children.

item.title: Melania Trump Repositions the White Suit
item.author: Vanessa Friedman
item.content:encoded: The first lady wore a white suit to preside over the White House meeting of delegations from Russia and Ukraine.
